facts.title: uncontrolled movement of P-7110 during a planned shutdown

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was first aid or minor property damage. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 1 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control EMERGENCY_ISOLATION_ON_RELEASE: the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment was not in place, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

Control HYDROCARBON_TRANSFER_CONTROL: the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels was in place but did not perform, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip was never verified as effective, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system was in place but did not perform, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

recommendations: Confirm at the next spot check that the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment on P-7110, M-7110 and TK-7101 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment, specifically setting and proving mechanical seal support systems. P-7110 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during a planned shutdown while the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment was not in place. The thermal energy involved is held as hot surface, and the recorded presentation was burn, ignition, scald.
response.summary: On 1 March 2007 an incident occurred on P-7110, M-7110 and TK-7101 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during a planned shutdown, releasing thermal energy held as hot surface.
